1.e4 c5 2.Nf3 Nc6 3.Nc3 e5 4.Bc4.strategy: Puts the bishop on its most active square, eyeing f7, where Black can no longer shield the diagonal with an e-pawn move. With the pawns on c5 and e5, neither covers d5, which stays a long-term outpost for White.

1.e4 c5 2.Nf3 Nc6 3.Nc3 e5 4.Bc4 Be7.strategy: A solid developing move that prepares castling and guards g5, so White's knight cannot jump there to double the attack on f7. Black keeps the structure intact and waits, accepting a modest game in which White controls d5.
